description: We chose the NASA Space Mission Design Game challenge to create an interactive simulation that makes space exploration easy to understand. By letting players build their own missions and manage realistic resources like budget, mass, and power, our game bridges the gap between complex engineering theory and hands-on fun for everyone.
summary: We developed an educational 2D space-mission game in Godot that lets players experience how real missions are designed, launched and operated. Solo or in teams of up to four, players take on roles and build a CubeSat under real constraints: budget, mass, power, battery reserve, electrical inhibitors and shielding against solar storms. They then choose a rocket and orbit, face a launch-timing challenge, and receive a report that explains in plain language why the mission succeeded or failed. After launch, they explore an interactive Moon base, manage the ship’s battery and condition, and run the BioNutrients experiment through hands-on tasks such as preparing water, using a syringe and injecting into a production bag. By turning complex engineering and safety rules into decisions players can see and feel, the game makes STEM concepts accessible, encourages teamwork and inspires the next generation of space scientists. It is available in Spanish and English.
details:
What exactly does it do?

Space Misions is an interactive, turn-based educational role-playing and simulation game that guides players through the complete lifecycle of designing, budgeting, and launching a space mission. Specifically:

  • It digitizes and simulates the authentic NASA systems engineering lifecycle and CubeSat 101 pedagogical frameworks into an accessible game environment.
  • It distributes responsibilities among players across four specialized rotating roles (Scientist, Engineer, Planner, and Financial Officer) to manage collaborative team decisions.
  • It integrates scientific payloads, allowing teams to choose primary scientific missions and specialized secondary modules such as the microgravity "Bionutrientes" astrobiology experiment.
  • It balances complex physical trade-offs in real time, managing payload mass limits, budget caps ($150 limit), power generation via solar arrays, and communication hardware.
  • It executes an arcade-style precision timing minigame for the rocket launch sequence, determining orbital insertion success and science multipliers.
  • It evaluates mission performance through a star-based rating report and detailed educational feedback, ensuring that biological and technical mission requirements are met.

How does it work?

The gameplay follows a structured, multi-phase engineering workflow:

  1. Setup & Role Assignment: Players choose the number of participants (1 to 4) and understand the rotating professional roles required for space mission development.
    • Scientist selects instruments (Cameras, Spectrometers, or the Bionutrientes Kit).
    • Engineer adds power sources (solar panels) and communication arrays, balancing power generation against power consumption.
  2. Launch Vehicle & Orbital Mechanics: The Planner chooses a rocket launcher and an orbit (Low, Medium, or High Earth Orbit), factoring in how orbital distance reduces effective payload capacity due to fuel penalties.
  3. Technical Approval & Launch: The Financial Officer reviews total mass and budget viability. Once approved, players execute the timing minigame to achieve a successful rocket liftoff.
  4. Mission Report: The system analyzes the final configuration, verifying if secondary experiments (like bionutrientes) received sufficient net energy to succeed, and generates a final score report.

What benefits does it have?

  • Educational & Pedagogical: Democratizes complex aerospace engineering concepts, teaching students about resource management, physical trade-offs, and systems thinking.
  • Collaborative & Social: Encourages teamwork and communication through structured turn-based mechanics.
  • Engaging & Replayable: Combines strategic resource allocation with a high-stakes arcade launch mechanic, ensuring high replay value for classrooms and workshops.

What do you hope to achieve?

In the short term, our goal is to provide students, educators, and space enthusiasts with an interactive tool that demystifies space mission design and highlights cutting-edge space biology research like microgravity plant cultivation. In the long term, we seek to inspire the next generation of engineers and scientists by making aerospace project management intuitive, engaging, and globally accessible.
